newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal LePage survey finds vacancies down.
newsitem.headline: Royal LePage survey finds vacancies down.

text.p: Royal LePage Ltd said on Thursday its survey of commercial real estate market conditions across Canada found vacancy rates continued to decline in the first quarter of 1997.

The Toronto-based real estate company said a study of the commercial real estate markets in nine Canadian cities found an average vacancy rate of 12.8 percent. A similar study of eight cities done at the end of 1996 found an average vacancy rate of 13.7 percent.
The survey found Toronto was by far the most active real estate market, with the vacancy rate falling to 12.4 percent from 14.4 percent.

"We see this as an extremely positive statement about Metro's (Toronto's) economy and even though we expect the pace of absorption in the Toronto marketplace to slow down, we are predicting a record year for office space absorption in the Toronto marketplace," John O'Bryan, a senior vice president with Royal LePage Commercial Inc, said in a statement.
O'Bryan said Toronto saw the biggest single quarterly absorption of commerical real estate this decade in the first quarter.

Other Canadian cities which saw vacancy rates fall included Ottawa, where rate fell to 12.3 percent from 13.5 percent and Montreal, where the rate fell to 16.1 percent from 16.6 percent. Vancouver's vacancy rate fell to 6.9 percent from 7.0 percent, and Calgary's fell to 9.1 percent from 9.7 percent.
Vancancy rates rose in Edmonton and Winnipeg in the first quarter, and remained steady in Regina.
